segs.e: “Mendicants, phoenixes reproduce in these four ways.

segs.p: Aṇḍajā supaṇṇā, jalābujā supaṇṇā, saṁsedajā supaṇṇā, opapātikā supaṇṇā—
segs.e: Phoenixes are born from eggs, from a womb, from moisture, or spontaneously.
These are the four ways that phoenixes reproduce.”
“Mendicants, phoenixes reproduce in these four ways.
Phoenixes are born from eggs, from a womb, from moisture, or spontaneously.
These are the four ways that phoenixes reproduce.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, aṇḍajā supaṇṇā aṇḍajeva nāge haranti, na jalābuje, na saṁsedaje, na opapātike.
segs.e: Of these, phoenixes born from an egg can only carry off dragons born from an egg, not those born from a womb, from moisture, or spontaneously.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, jalābujā supaṇṇā aṇḍaje ca jalābuje ca nāge haranti, na saṁsedaje, na opapātike.
segs.e: Phoenixes born from a womb can carry off dragons born from an egg or from a womb, but not those born from moisture or spontaneously.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, saṁsedajā supaṇṇā aṇḍaje ca jalābuje ca saṁsedaje ca nāge haranti, na opapātike.
segs.e: Phoenixes born from moisture can carry off dragons born from an egg, from a womb, or from moisture, but not those born spontaneously.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, opapātikā supaṇṇā aṇḍaje ca jalābuje ca saṁsedaje ca opapātike ca nāge haranti.
segs.e: Phoenixes born spontaneously can carry off dragons born from an egg, from a womb, from moisture, or spontaneously.
These are the four ways that phoenixes reproduce.”

segs.p: Aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṁ supaṇṇānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why someone, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in the company of the egg-born phoenixes?”

segs.p: “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena dvayakārī hoti, vācāya dvayakārī, manasā dvayakārī.
segs.e: “Mendicant, it’s when someone does both kinds of deeds by body, speech, and mind.
‘The egg-born phoenixes are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’

segs.p: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṁ supaṇṇānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
segs.e: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the egg-born phoenixes!’

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṁ supaṇṇānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the egg-born phoenixes.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā aṇḍajānaṁ supaṇṇānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī”ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why someone, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in the company of the egg-born phoenixes.”
